hard_failures: HF-A2-19-01: the file registered as node A2's artifact (evaluation/ablation.csv, sha256 ee3aa6cb97d0 = the controller's measured A2 pin) is an unmarked synthetic dry-run: its header carries no simulation/status/provenance column, its numbers are the synthetic run of evaluation/ablation_harness.py (generator df878e97), and the design's artifact inventory (design lines 170-175) names only evaluation/ablation_dryrun.csv. The card's falsifier therefore fires: the dry-run can be reported as a real matched-budget comparison.

HF-A2-19-02: the pre-registration is not single-sourced to one executable rule. The design names artifacts/audit/ablation_harness.py (line 172, sha ee0d87a1) while the card/map register evaluation/ablation_harness.py (sha df878e97); the two differ. The design requires +/-2% on tokens and wall clock (lines 46-49); the small harness uses audit_lib.check_budget_match tol=0.02, the big harness DEFAULTS token_tolerance=0.15, and the big harness checks no wall-clock spread at all. Two of the four declared matched fields (line 58: verifier_calls_per_accepted_artifact, human_review_minutes) appear nowhere in either harness or any output.

HF-A2-19-03: the NULL arm id does not survive the design's own YAML loader. Line 40 is `- id: NULL` unquoted, so yaml.safe_load (the loader used by evaluation/ablation_harness.py:436-444 for --design) yields None, not the string "NULL"; any consumer that keys arms by id cannot address the one mandatory control the card asks about.
acceptance: Verdict cites 1b2a83ef670b; independent text; explicitly states design-only vs executed; null baseline exists; dry-run cannot be mistaken for a real arm result.

dryrun_not_mistakable_for_real.detail: the design-named dryrun files are labelled (report status SIMULATED; filenames contain dryrun) and --execute is fail-closed, but the artifact registered on node A2 is an unmarked dry-run CSV; design inventory does not cover it (HF-01)

falsifier: A design that would let the dry-run be reported as a real matched-budget comparison.

findings.finding: evaluation/ablation.csv sha256 ee3aa6cb97d0871a526102654fb9a793680c9f7e4f0ef3958b0a8db3648e8d45 is the dry-run table of evaluation/ablation_harness.py: its rows equal the synthetic arms in evaluation/ablation_report.json (generator_sha256 df878e97, assignment 'synthetic dry-run only, no model calls'). Its 23-column header contains no sim/synthetic/dry/status/provenance/generator marker (probe A2-14), while the design names only evaluation/ablation_dryrun.csv (sha bda738ff) and evaluation/ablation_dryrun_report.json (sha e1860fa1). The same hash ee3aa6cb is recorded as the controller's measured A2 pin (runtime/state/controller_verification/astra-lifecycle-06-decisions.json, measured_pins.A2).
findings.remedy: Add machine-readable provenance to tabular outputs (status=SIMULATED, generator_sha256, design_sha256) or rename to *_dryrun.csv, and repoint the node-A2 artifact to the design-labelled file; reserve evaluation/runs/ for real runs only.

findings.finding: Two byte-different harnesses exist for one pre-registered design: artifacts/audit/ablation_harness.py (sha ee0d87a1, named at line 172) and evaluation/ablation_harness.py (sha df878e97, the card's evidence ref and the generator of the registered artifacts). They disagree on the rule under review: audit_lib.check_budget_match tol=0.02 (audit_lib.py:404) vs big-harness DEFAULTS token_tolerance=0.15 (ablation_harness.py:75). The big harness's check_matched_budgets (lines 384-422) enforces no wall-clock spread tolerance (only per-arm overspend and wall_clock stop_reason), and neither harness nor output emits verifier_calls_per_accepted_artifact or human_review_minutes (probe A2-10), i.e. 2 of the 4 matched fields at line 58 are unmeasured.
findings.remedy: Single-source the harness path in design + map; put numeric token_tolerance and wall_tolerance fields in the design and read them from there; add a wall-clock spread check; emit and check all four matched fields or reduce matched_fields to those actually enforced.

findings.finding: `- id: NULL` is unquoted, so the YAML 1.1 loader used by the harness for --design (evaluation/ablation_harness.py:436-444, yaml.safe_load) parses the id as None. Probe A2-03b measured parsed_id=null. The design is supposed to be hashed and consumed before execution (line 97), so the mandatory control arm is not addressable by its declared id.

The design specifies NULL as 'iid random selection from the task's candidate pool at the same token spend, plus a shuffled-gate control'. The design-named harness simulates NULL as an ordinary declared-rate arm (SIM['NULL'] = {p_accept: 0.06, tokens_per_call: 2137, hf: 0.16}; artifacts/audit/ablation_harness.py:36) and its report admits 'here it is a declared low-acceptance arm' (ablation_dryrun_report.json:154). The dry-run therefore exercises a placeholder, not the specified control (probe A2-17).
findings.remedy: Implement the iid candidate-pool sampler and shuffled-gate control behind the same interface, or mark the NULL slot in the dry-run explicitly as unimplemented rather than as a rate.

findings.finding: In evaluation/ablation_report.json the random_iid_null arm consumed 3000 of its 20000-token budget and stopped with episodes_exhausted (probe A2-18), and the report's own limitation says 'the iid null arm exhausts the episode suite before its token budget, so its consumption is not token-matched'. Design falsifier item 3 (line 167) voids a comparison whose NULL arm got a different budget.
findings.remedy: Define the NULL stop rule (resample with replacement to the same token cap) and make check_matched_budgets treat a non-token-exhausted NULL as a violation for the primary comparison, or scope NULL comparisons explicitly.

findings.finding: The declared decision rule applies the hard-failure guardrail first. The dry-run computes primary contrasts from the raw summary (artifacts/audit/ablation_harness.py:162-167) and reports arms_above=[IC, NULL] with no truncation (ablation_dryrun_report.json:126-132), so the exercised pipeline does not implement the rule it reports against. 'its accepted count is truncated at the gate' (line 106) is also not a machine-defined operation, so the guardrail cannot be tested as written.
findings.remedy: Define the truncation function numerically, apply it before contrasts, and add a self-test asserting that an arm above 0.10 has its reported accepted count truncated.

findings.finding: Exit status is not a reliable signal in either direction: with --outdir outside the repo root the harness writes both artifacts and then exits 1 with ValueError from the final relative_to (probe A2-19: files written before failure); with a provider config present --execute exits 0 while doing no work ('only the dry-run scheduler is implemented in this harness revision'). A CI wrapper keying on exit status reads a completed dry-run as failed and a no-op as succeeded.
findings.remedy: Print the path without relative_to (or guard it), and return a distinct nonzero code for 'execute not implemented'.

findings.finding: The design-named dry-run CSV has no in-file simulated flag; the only marker is the filename. This is tolerable for ablation_dryrun.csv but is the same gap that produced HF-A2-19-01 for the sibling evaluation/ablation.csv.
findings.remedy: Emit a provenance preamble/column (status, generator_sha256, design_sha256) in every tabular output.

findings.finding: Confirmed on the pinned bytes: the design declares a NULL control arm with role 'mandatory control' and a matching falsifier; it forbids a universal scalar score by construction; it states the +/-2% matched-budget rule and four matched fields; it pre-registers 8 seeds, a power warning that n=8 cannot detect +3%, and four design-level falsifiers; execution_status is blocked. The design-named harness replay reproduces the registered evaluation/ablation_dryrun.csv byte-identically (sha bda738ff) and its report content modulo generated_at, and --execute refuses without a provider config (exit 3, no file writes) - probe A2-11 and A2-12.
findings.remedy: None; these are the parts to preserve in revision.
